metadata.note: The Orange and Alexandria Railroad (1851-1872, renamed Orange, Alexandria and Manassas in 1867), the Washington City, Virginia Midland and Great Southern / Virginia Midland Railway (1873-1886), and the Richmond and Danville (1886-1894) and Southern Railway (1894 on) on the branches. One feature per drawable span and operator; features for different operators over the same track share identical geometry (Rule 4 splits). The Southern-era main line (1891 on) is drawn by southern_railway_crescent.geojson and is not repeated; the Manassas Gap Railroad's own pre-June-1867 line is its own report and is not repeated; Washington - Alexandria (Alexandria and Washington / Long Bridge, another company's track) is not drawn in these colours.
sources: Alexandria Gazette, Baltimore Daily Commercial, Richmond Daily Dispatch, Staunton Spectator, Evening Star, Spirit of Jefferson, Herald and Tribune (Jonesborough TN) timetable ads, via loc.gov (Chronicling America) page OCR
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952
metadata.rule_1_exclusions: Not drawn: US Military Railroads operation 1862-1865 (Alexandria - Manassas - Warrenton - Culpeper - Rapidan; troop and supply trains, no public timetable); any O&A line in 1864 - Aug 1865 (no public train proven); the Alexandria waterfront / Wilkes Street tunnel spur (freight only); Orange - Gordonsville after the 1880 cutoff as a VM line (freight station list only); the Pigg River iron-mines branch; the Feb 1952 Guide's freight-only Tables 33 and 34. Also not drawn: the B&O-era Strasburg - Harrisonburg (about 1873 to 1894-98; a different company); the 1914-1932 county-run Franklin and Pittsylvania.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN END - Warrenton Branch, Southern era: last confirmed 1938 (Sunday trains off); freight-only by Feb 1952. A 1939-1950 'last train' item or SCC order would settle it.
OPEN END - Warrenton Branch, pre-war O&A: confirmed only 1853-1854; 1855-1861 timetables naming Warrenton not found.
OPEN END - Charlottesville - Lynchburg, Confederate era: last confirmed Sept 1863; 1864-65 probable.

OPEN END - Orange - Gordonsville - Charlottesville, Virginia Midland: last confirmed 1874; whether through trains used Gordonsville or the 1880 cutoff in 1880-1885 is unread, so neither route is drawn for the VM in 1875-1886.
OPEN END - Franklin Division, Southern era: last confirmed 1904; the lease ran to 1914.
OPEN START - Strasburg Junction - Harrisonburg, Southern era: first confirmed 1898; the B&O-to-Southern change falls in 1894-1898.
Franklin Division start: proven only from 1885 (built and leased 1880).
Lynchburg - Danville first train (late 1873 or early 1874) not found; drawn from 1874.
Manassas Junction opening (1851 vs Jan 1852) and Orange opening (late 1853 vs Mar 1854) not established; drawn from the confirmed years.
Rapidan - Culpeper in 1863 and the whole Confederate-side line in 1864: probable, unproven, not drawn.
1941 application to suspend Manassas - Harrisonburg trains 11/12: outcome not checked.
John S. Barbour as O&A president from the 1850s is from memory in the report and not sourced.
All headway_min values are estimates read from the advertised number of trains; avg_speed_kmh is computed from an ad where speed_source says so, otherwise estimated.
metadata.existing_layer_defects: southern_railway_crescent.geojson (southern-crescent) draws 1891-1893 in Southern colour although the Richmond and Danville ran the corridor until 1 Jul 1894 (Rule 4). Not edited here; this layer's R&D main line stops at 1890 so the two do not overlap.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 63.1 mi against 63.6 mi documented (-0.8%). [manassas frontroyal: 50.0 mi drawn vs 51.0 mi, Fowler line 4, MP 32.6-83.6] OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=Southern (NS B-Line, the Manassas Gap Railroad's line). Modern alignment; realignments not checked. [frontroyal strasjct: 13.1 mi drawn vs 12.6 mi, Fowler line 4, MP 83.6-96.2] OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=Southern (NS B-Line) through Riverton (the Shenandoah Valley / N&W crossing) to Strasburg and on about 1 mi to Strasburg Junction. Strasburg Junction is placed by Nominatim (locality); the 1885 and 1892 ads name Strasburg, the 1874 ad Strasburg Junction, and the drawn line runs to the Junction for all eras. Manassas - Strasburg - Harrisonburg was traced as one chain and split at the vertices nearest Front Royal (town-centre geocode, 1.4 km off the line) and Strasburg Junction, so the split between the first two pieces is about 0.5 mi from Fowler's Front Royal milepost; the two together draw 63.1 mi against 63.6 documented. No straight-line legs.

segments.note: Southern Railway from 1 Jul 1894 (R&D anchors 1886 and 1892 on the other side). Through Washington - Harrisonburg trains with buffet parlor cars in Dec 1914; July 1917 cuts made 21/14 daily-except-Sunday; Washington - Manassas through running cut 1940-41 (a 1941 application to suspend 11/12 has an unestablished outcome). Ends 1947: the Virginia SCC let the Southern discontinue trains 11 and 12, Manassas - Harrisonburg, from midnight 4 Jan 1948 (Evening Star 19 Dec 1947); 1948 itself is not drawn. Feb 1952 Guide Table 33: freight service only. Headway is an estimate read from the advertised number of trains, not a measured interval.

segments.note: [OPEN start] Drawn from 1898, the first CONFIRMED year of Southern trains here, not a known start: a B&O timetable printed Aug 1898 has 'Train 59 connects with Southern R. R. at Strasburg Junction ... for Harrisonburg' (its effective date, possibly June 1897, is unreadable in the OCR). The B&O still ran it in 1893 (Fowler's B&O timetable letters) and the Southern absorbed the lease in 1894 (virginiaplaces); when the B&O's trains stopped and the Southern's began within 1894-1898 is not established. Do not move the start earlier without evidence. July 1917 cuts dropped trains 49/24 Strasburg - Harrisonburg. Ends 1947 (trains 11/12 discontinued from 4 Jan 1948). Headway is an estimate read from the advertised number of trains, not a measured interval.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 32.1 mi against 37.0 mi documented (-13.2%). [franklin: 32.1 mi drawn vs 37.0 mi, Fowler line 88; virginiaplaces says '30-mile'] Lifted after 1932. Gretna (Franklin Junction) - about 2 mi west of Sandy Level (13.9 mi) traced over the one OSM way tagged old_railway_operator=Franklin and Pittsylvania (way 169913857, itself tagged fixme 'rough alignment in places'), joined to the main line by a 0.5 mi straight connector at Gretna. West of the end of that way nothing is mapped in OSM or OpenHistoricalMap (OHM returned no railway ways in 36.85,-79.95,37.05,-79.30), so the rest is STRAIGHT LINES between town centres: mapped end - Penhook 3.35 mi, Penhook - Union Hall 3.07 mi, Union Hall - Glade Hill 4.08 mi (Glade Hill placed only approximately, from a Nominatim hit on Glade Hill Cemetery), Glade Hill - Rocky Mount 7.25 mi; 17.75 mi straight in all, about half the line. The short-cut chords are why the drawn line is about 13% under the documented 37.0 mi.

segments.note: Southern Railway lessee from 1894. Rocky Mount appears beside Franklin Junction in the Southern main-line timetable of May 1904 (Staunton Spectator and Vindicator 13 May 1904; times not attributable in the OCR). [OPEN] This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. The lease ran to 1914, when the Southern let it expire; the county-run railroad of 1914-1932 is a separate operator, not researched and not drawn. 1932 is that railroad's shutdown, not a passenger end for the Southern. Headway is an estimate read from the advertised number of trains, not a measured interval.
sources: Segment-level: research report block [17] (VM ad of 22 Mar 1885 'Franklin Division'; R&D Mar 1892 tri-weekly schedule; Rocky Mount in the Southern timetable of May 1904).
